Multi-site industrial distribution

The OTIF problem was not in the warehouse

How a 16-branch network moved OTIF from 60% to 85% by fixing promise logic, measurement and exception management.

16branches
60%starting OTIF
85%OTIF after 12 months
£0capital investment required

The situation

A UK industrial distribution business operating 16 branches had sustained OTIF performance around 60%. The previous improvement programme had focused almost entirely on warehouse operations.

The score was real. The question was whether it was locating the cause.

What the journey showed

Promise dates were set without branch-level stock position, so orders reached branches already late. OTIF also stopped at despatch rather than delivery, creating a gap between the internal score and the customer experience.

The rebuild

Promise logic began drawing from live stock, the OTIF definition moved to delivery confirmation and a daily exception review covered orders already at risk before the branch received them.

Measured result

Within twelve months, OTIF moved from 60% to 85%. No capital investment was required and no headcount change was made.

Historical operator track record. Company name withheld. Metrics and factual framing follow the confirmed September 2026 case-study source.
